compliance.notes: Technically competent, commissioner-overseen TMSS: the core prudential indicators are all present with figures - strongest on capital expenditure/CFR (full year-on-year CFR bridge), the borrowing strategy (clear internal-borrowing/under-borrowing narrative), a properly constructed four-balance liability benchmark chart, the MRP policy statement, and a robust creditworthiness policy using CDS beyond ratings. Weakest area is commercial/non-treasury investment disclosure relative to the size of the legacy 0.9bn book: proportionality is acknowledged but not demonstrated (COM-03 core), the new commercial-income-to-net-revenue indicator is absent (PI-08), and IMPs, the paras 51-53 compliance statement, a quantitative portfolio-risk indicator, an ESG policy, separate HRA/GF benchmarks and an audit-qualification flag are all missing. Overall a compliant recovery-phase strategy whose gaps cluster in the commercial-investment and secondary-disclosure requirements.

news_drafts.headline: Thurrock's budget depends on emergency government money as asset sales and building programmes slip.
news_drafts.lead: Thurrock Council set a balanced 2026/27 budget only by assuming £68.9m of exceptional financial support from government — money to cover treasury costs and operational deficit that the council cannot otherwise afford. This emergency backing reveals how deeply the authority depends on two promised routes to financial recovery: selling assets and delivering capital projects. Both are failing. The asset disposal programme is on track to raise only £12.2m of a £25.3m budget, a shortfall of 52%. The capital programme, after slipping £87.5m (73% of budget) in 2025/26, is already forecasting a £15.6m underspend (20% of budget) in the first quarter of the new year. Commissioners, who now oversee the council, have required stronger governance and stricter oversight on complex schemes. The council holds reserves to manage pressures but is drawing them down — £17.9m planned for 2026/27 — rather than closing the underlying gap.

findings.headline: Earmarked reserves reduced by £11.1m net whilst general balance maintained at £11m
findings.detail: The council makes gross draw-downs of £17.9m from earmarked reserves whilst receiving contributions of £6.8m, resulting in net reduction of £11.1m. The unallocated General Balance remains unchanged at £11.000m. Total General Fund reserves fall from £85.9m to £74.9m.
findings.matters: For a lender, maintenance of the general balance during substantial net draw-down of earmarked reserves shows the council retains a financial buffer. However, deployment of reserves at this scale to meet ongoing service costs indicates structural budget pressures rather than one-off costs.
findings.figures: Earmarked reserves fall from £74.949m to £63.873m; General Balance £11.000m (unchanged); net draw from earmarked reserves £11.076m
findings.quote: Total Earmarked Reserves: Balance as at 31 March 2026 £74.949m ... Forecast Balance as at 31 March 2027 £63.873m

findings.headline: Children's safeguarding reserve increased by £0.2m whilst adult services reserves exhausted
findings.detail: Whilst adult social care reserves are completely drawn down, the council contributes £0.2m to strengthen its Safeguarding Vulnerable People (children) reserve, increasing the balance from £0.01m to £0.26m. This represents a deliberate allocation choice to build capacity in children's safeguarding at the same time adult services are consuming all available reserves.
findings.matters: The pattern shows emerging pressures in children's services requiring proactive reserve-building at the same time adult services are drawing down all designated reserves. It signals the council is managing competing demands across age groups and may indicate shifting pressures to children's services.
findings.quote: This funding will support the safeguarding and the welfare of children through preventative, proactive and responsive activity

findings.headline: Adult social care reserves of £9.9m entirely depleted across six funding streams
findings.detail: The council completely draws down six reserves designated for adult social care in 2026-27: the Better Care Fund (£5.8m), Adults c/f Reserve (£0.4m), Market Sustainability Funding (£0.7m), ASC-Health integration (£1.2m), Supporting Families (£0.3m), and Adult Social Care Reserve (£1.5m) created in December 2024 specifically for demographic pressures. The ASC draw-downs represent 89% of the council's total £11.1m net draw from all earmarked reserves. The December 2024 reserve created to address population growth is fully consumed within one financial year.
findings.matters: Complete draw-down of service-specific reserves signals that permanent operational savings have not closed underlying budget gaps and costs are being managed through reserve depletion. For a lender or finance director at another council, this reveals that at this rate of draw-down (£11m annually), the council would exhaust its earmarked reserves within 6-7 years without spending reductions or additional funding.
findings.figures: Better Care Fund £5.772m, Adults c/f £0.400m, Market Sustainability £0.693m, ASC-Health integration £1.204m, Supporting Families £0.291m, ASC Reserve £1.500m
findings.quote: New Reserve created for ASC/CS demographic pressures as agreed at December 2024 Cabinet

findings.headline: General Fund capital programme slippage of £15.624m forecast for 2026/27 despite Q1 review
findings.detail: Despite completion of a Q1 review of the capital programme following significant 2025/26 slippage (£87.462m, 73% of budget), the General Fund capital programme is forecast to underspend by £15.624m (20% of £75.944m budget) in 2026/27. The majority of slippage is in Place directorate (£14.651m). A review released £0.712m of funds and enhanced monthly monitoring has been introduced.
findings.matters: Persistent capital slippage affects delivery of strategic outcomes and signals capability issues in programme delivery.
findings.figures: £15.624m forecast underspend (20% of revised budget) in 2026/27, £87.462m underspend in 2025/26, £81.900m of that slippage, £14.651m slippage in Place forecast for 2026/27
findings.quote: The General Fund Capital Programme is forecast to underspend by £15.624m (20%) against a revised budget of £75.944m due to slippage.

findings.headline: Asset disposal receipts forecast at £12.191m against £25.320m budget for 2026/27
findings.detail: Total capital receipts from asset disposals for 2026/27 are currently forecast at £12.191m against a budget of £25.320m, representing only 48% of target. Only £4.025m has been realised to date in Q1. The asset disposal programme remains critical to the council's debt reduction strategy and medium-term financial sustainability, and the shortfall could impact borrowing requirements and debt reduction trajectory.
findings.matters: Asset disposal shortfalls mean higher borrowing requirements and reduced debt reduction capability in the council's recovery strategy.
findings.figures: £12.191m forecast receipts against £25.320m budget for 2026/27, £4.025m realised to date, £13.129m shortfall, revised plan £104.100m to be delivered by end 2027/28
findings.quote: Total receipts for 2026/27 are currently forecast at £12.191m against a budget of £25.320m.
